Citizens wishing to address the City Council and Successor Agency on any item on the agenda or on any matter

Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda .

at the time the item is considered by the City Council. If you wish to address the City Council /Successor Agency
at this time, please complete a speaker's card and give it to the City Clerk prior to commencement of the City
Council meeting. Please limit your remarks to three (3) minutes.

To increase the effectiveness of the Public Comment Period, the following rules shall be followed: No person
shall make any remarks which result in disrupting, disturbing or otherwise impeding the meeting.

Pursuant to Section 54957.95 of the Government Code, the presiding member of the legislative body conducting
a meeting, or their designee, is authorized to remove, or cause the removal of, an individual for disrupting the
meeting. Any such removal will be preceded by a warning to the disruptive individual by the presiding member of
the legislative body or their designee that the individual ’s behavior is disrupting the meeting and that the
individual’s failure to promptly cease their disruptive behavior may result in their removal.

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
CALL TO ORDER Mayor Altamirano called meeting to order at 10:05 a.m.

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS Deputy City Attorney Almazan announced that, due to multiple speakers and in accordance with the Brown Act, each speaker would be limited to one minute.

Lela Leon asked that full-time positions not be converted to part-time.

Jesse Hernandez questioned why recreation programs are being reduced and suggested finding alternative budget cuts rather than eliminating positions.

Ethan Baltierra, Silvia Muñoz, and Antonia Lupercio voiced opposition to proposed position eliminations.

Sonia Griego spoke about her career path with the City and urged that her position not be eliminated.

Grace Baltierra, a preschool teacher and recreation leader, stated that it is unfair to eliminate the position held by her mother, Rachel Baltierra, who served over 20 years as Aquatics Program Manager.

Rachel Baltierra stated she has been full-time for over 20 years and that the City of Commerce helped shape her career.

Charles Baltierra read a letter from Ernie Cardenas opposing the elimination of Rachel Baltierra’s position.

Support for Maintaining Full-Time Aquatics/Swim Coach Position:

Erika Burgos asked that athletic programs not be taken away, noting her son is a competitive swimmer.

Alexa Jimenez, Erika Silva, Ayelen Jimenez - participants in the swimming program, said eliminating the full-time position is a mistake and part-time staffing would be inadequate.

Scarleth Carcamo expressed concern about the future of her children, supported keeping the full-time coach, and urged funding to improve programs.

Melvin Carcamo, a swimming participant, said a successful coach is key to achieving success and asked to keep the full-time position.

Arcenio Tagorda, and Eli Tagorda, a swim and polo athletes, spoke in support of keeping the full-time coach.

Cecilia Gonzalez and Janelle Ocampo opposed eliminating the full-time coach position.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council recessed to Closed Session at 10:38 a.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council reconvened to open session at 11:18pm

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT Deputy City Attorney Almazan reported that, with the entire Council present, the City Council discussed two potential litigation items during Closed Session, and no reportable action was taken.


Mayor Altamirano and Councilmember Rebollo explained that public comments were taken prior to the Closed Session because the Closed Session item was directly related to an Open Session item, and the Council wanted to provide everyone the opportunity to be heard. Mayor Altamirano stated that programs will be enhanced, not reduced.




CALL TO ORDER

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT Alfredo Beltran. AFSCME Local, stated that the goal of restructuring should be clear and not overlook the individuals affected. He noted that the transition would be difficult and emphasized the importance of working together to ensure a smooth process.




SCHEDULED MATTERS

3.. Gateway Cities Regional Fiber Optic Network Project City Manager Hernandez asked to continue to the next meeting.

4.. Presentation Regarding Digital Billboards This item was continued to the next meeting.

2.. Implementation of Organizational Restructuring  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Hugo Argumedo City Manager Ernie Hernandez stated that, during the recent budget process and analysis, it was discovered that the Recreation Department had been over budget by more than $2 million in each of the past three years. He noted that the City also needs to subsidize the transit program and that, without Measure AA funding, there would be no Capital Improvement Programs. This process, he explained, includes identifying efficiencies with the goal of enhancing or maintaining services. 
City Manager Hernandez recommended that the City Council approve the salary changes outlined in Exhibit D and stated that the changes would take about a month to implement.

Mayor Altamirano reiterated that the City’s swim program is ranked number one in the nation and is well-known nationwide. He guaranteed that the program would be enhanced, noting that additional improvements are planned. He further stated that if the program suffers in any way, the City Manager will be held accountable, and adjustments will be made.

Councilmember Rebollo reiterated that employee matters cannot be discussed from the dais, which is why the City Council took public comments prior to the Closed Session. Councilmember Rebollo commended every parent and athlete in attendance, acknowledging that these decisions are not easy, but emphasized that they are made with a commitment to improve the program and the community. She added that it is the Council’s responsibility to safeguard the community.



ADJOURNMENT Meeting adjourned at 11:34 a.m.
